rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes only a comment text from 'Load 4 elements at once using float4' to 'Load 3 elements at once using float4' on line 17. Comments are stripped during CUDA compilation and have zero effect on the generated PTX/machine code. The actual executable kernel code (all arithmetic, control flow, memory operations) remains identical byte-for-byte.
rounds.survival_reason: This mutation modifies only a comment within the CUDA source string. When the CUDA compiler processes this source, it discards all comments during preprocessing, producing identical object code. The mutation tool detected a change to the constant '4' but this constant appears only inside a C++ comment, not in executable code. Layer 2's 112 rounds of dynamic testing confirmed bitwise equivalence across all test patterns because the compiled kernels are identical. No input values can distinguish outputs from identical machine code.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable. The mutation affects only a comment, which is not compiled into executable code. The CUDA compiler produces identical kernels for both original and mutant. No value-level input can expose any behavioral difference because the underlying machine code is identical.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should filter out comment-only mutations before reporting them as potentially killable. Static analysis at Layer 0/1 should strip comments and compare actual code tokens to immediately identify such equivalent mutants without needing dynamic testing rounds.
